item: D-173 A design: AC9 load-rule amendment
non_blocking: N1 (AC3 drill block incomplete): drill() runs `sh "$T/mutate-$m.sh"` but $T is a fresh mktemp dir and only `cp -R tools` populates it; the mutate-*.sh scripts are never copied in, so every mutant would exit 2 as written. The comment says the executor writes them, but the block is described as saved verbatim. Likewise the `rig` half (AC4-AC10 commands) is comments only, so those commands are not runnable until the executor writes it. The doc says so honestly; the single-case mode the drill relies on does exist (tools/test_suite_profile.sh line ~300, `[ "$#" = 1 ]`).

N2 (markdown-escaped pipes): AC2, AC11, AC13, AC15 commands contain `\|` in the raw file. Run literally, `printf 'a\nb\n' | grep -c -E '^(a\|b)$'` prints 0 on macOS grep (the unescaped form prints 2). Fine once rendered; wrong if copied from source. AC11 with real pipes, run by me against $TMPDIR/rig-check, printed `basis-gate ui-theme-check` three times, as claimed.

N3 (E can under-read by H rounding): the proof shows R(w) <= actual run CPU, but E = H - R and H is iostat whole-percent us+sy, so E can under-read true outside load by up to about 1 percent of ncpu = 0.16 cores per window (before damping). The slack s only protects spare_k, not H. The goal text 'errs toward loaded in every window' is therefore true up to 0.16 cores. Immaterial against thresholds of 5 and 8, but not stated.

N4 (timestamp resolution): the prototype and the spec use integer epoch seconds (macOS date has no %N). Delta-t_k can then be off by about 1 s per interval, which understates spare_k (and so cap_L) by up to H x 1 s, more than s x dt (1.6 core-s) covers, in the unsafe direction for lb. Errors telescope (about 1 s total across a span), so the effect is at most roughly 0.3-0.5 cores in a 30-s window. The doc marks iostat/ps alignment UNMEASURED but does not specify the sub-second clock.

N5 (wrong direction in Step 2.5 caveat): the added sentence says misalignment 'can over-state spare_k only by the CPU that crossed the edge'. Over-stating spare_k is the safe direction; the unsafe one is understating it. The '5 s of 30' bound is the controller's own addition, not a reviewer fix. Also 'a larger spare only lowers the bound' (slack paragraph) is imprecise because cap_w in lb=min(cap_w, ...) rises with spare; soundness is unaffected since cap_w is not needed for lb <= unseen_L(w).

N6 (late-admitted members): the sampler writes C rows only for members, so a process first admitted as a member at snapshot k with CPU accumulated earlier has no prior baseline. Counted from zero it would put earlier CPU into O_k (timing shifted into window k, so R(w) could exceed the run's CPU in w). The spec does not say how a first-sighting member with lstart before the previous snapshot is baselined. Needs a rule (skip or baseline from a non-member snapshot) in A1a; reachable only through a multi-snapshot chain break followed by recovery, so rare.

N7 (interpretive departure, disclosed): D-173 A says 'count only load from processes outside the run, keeping the thresholds'. The doc keeps the numbers 5/8 but applies them to a damped CPU-core quantity E and demotes load1 to context (R4 states bursts of runnable threads no longer count; OQ1 asks Mark). Defensible and visible, but it is a change of the quantity the thresholds bound, and should be the first line Mark reads in OQ1. 'Depends on: D-173 answered A' also reads as if answered; the ledger row is still OPEN and the loop is following the default.

N8 (citation): Problem 3 cites a `wl` column `ewma_host` of analyse.sh, but the bundle has no wl.analyse.tsv; wl.analyse2.tsv has only a raw `host` column. I recomputed the 60-s-damped host from it (windows 5-12: diffs -0.14, 0.15, -0.06, 0.32, 0.31, 0.11, 0.12, 0.04, mean +0.106), matching the doc, but windows 1-4 differ by -2.7 to -0.25 (warm-up), which the 'steady state' wording hides.

N9 (LOC realism): A1a +45 lines for the CPU sampler (membership with sticky/group/lstart, N/C/H rows) and A1b +95 for the lower bound, U(L), refusals and keep-going look low against the 60-line prototype awk. The 270-line split has headroom but the estimate is optimistic.
N10 (AC12 command vague): 'scratch copies as in the finding's re-check' is not a runnable command by itself.

V26 re-read myself in the clone (HEAD e20175b5, rig_check.sh sha256 37defb61...c1516 matches): line 113 is `bounded "$TEST_S" sh tools/suite_profile.sh run --make gmake --out "$dir.profile" -- $trace -k test ...`; line 122 is the same with `--make make` (the gmake-missing fallback branch, not specifically a '3.81' branch, but it is the system make); bounded() forks, the child does setpgrp(0,0), reopens stdin, then execs @ARGV, so the exec'd suite_profile.sh shell is its own group leader (pgid = pid); the probe file shows pid=54004 pgid=54004 against a no-setpgrp control 54103/54094. The doc's claims about both lines and bounded() are accurate. Instrument runs from the clone at the sha (line 'needs the instrument on the PR head'), so A1a code takes effect for the nightly after it lands.

Lower-bound proof: Step 2.5 (H_k dt_k >= O_k + sum_L unseen_L(k), hence unseen_L(k) <= spare_k, and <= ncpu x overlap) is sound, including the boundary-interval and concurrent -j6 cases gemini raised, because O_k is real CPU used in k and unseen is additional disjoint CPU. Steps 1-4 then give lb_L(w) <= max(0, unseen_L(w)) and lower bounds add; cap_w is not needed for soundness. I could not construct a counterexample to R(w) <= actual run CPU under the stated assumptions (exact intervals, same-interval H, members really the run's); the gaps are N3-N6, all small or implementation-level.

summary: Pass, 85/100, no blocking findings. Every evidence reading in the doc re-derives: the tarball and SHA256SUMS hashes match, the public copy is byte-identical, all analyse3 and synthetic outputs are cmp-identical, and every quoted number I checked matches its file. The V26 claims about rig_check.sh lines 113 and 122 and bounded() are accurate. The lower-bound proof is sound once Step 2.5 is added (I confirmed it handles gemini's boundary and -j6 cases) and I found no counterexample to R(w) <= actual run CPU under the stated assumptions. The doc implements option A faithfully in substance (outside-the-run load, thresholds and median-of-three kept, keep-going red run counts only with an identical named failing set) and stops for Mark with default-if-unanswered 'stop'; the one interpretive step (thresholds now bound damped CPU cores, load1 not gated) is disclosed in R4 and OQ1 but should be more prominent. The carve-out was legitimate: no round-2 objection disputed option A or the rule's direction, and the revision-2 edits are the reviewers' own fixes (gemini fix (2), glm V26 plus citations, kimi AC13 check); the only controller-authored additions are small (the '5 s of 30' note, which also has the over/under-state direction backwards, and the not-triggered contingencies). Weaknesses are all non-blocking: the drill block and rig half are not runnable as saved (missing mutate scripts, comments-only rig function), markdown-escaped pipes in commands, E under-reads by up to about 0.16 cores from iostat rounding, integer-second timestamps and late-admitted-member baselining are unspecified, and the LOC estimates look low.
